chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not drink water from the notch of a vessel, nor from its handle, for Satan sits upon the handle and the notch.'

key_terms.ثُلْمَة: Notch or chipped part of a vessel's rim — a physical defect creating a gap in the lip
key_terms.عُرْوَة: Handle of a vessel, the looped protrusion used for gripping
key_terms.يَقْعُدُ: Sits/dwells — implying habitual or persistent spiritual presence

ai.seo_question: Why is it forbidden to drink from the handle or notch of a cup in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) transmits a directive of Imam Ali (AS) prohibiting drinking from the notch or handle of a vessel, citing the presence of Satan at those points. This hadith belongs to the Shia jurisprudential tradition of dining and drinking etiquette, where specific physical practices are linked to spiritual consequences. The early Muslim audience understood such prohibitions within a framework where ritual hygiene and demonic influence were closely interrelated.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Gayas Bin Ibrahim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Neither drink the water from a notch of the vessel, nor from its handle, for the Satan<sup>la</sup> sits upon the handle and the notch’.
en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that ’Amir al-Mu’minin has said, ‘Do not drink water from the broken part of a bowl or from its handle because Satan sits on the broken part and on the handle (ring).”’
